findings.title: SKILL.md.tmpl's shared body text is false when rendered for the gbg-doctor skill
locations: templates/SKILL.md.tmpl:7-11 — "opens the round, and prints this instrument's protocol, the exact `Workflow` call and the next step"
templates/SKILL.md.tmpl:15 — "Follow the protocol printed above, exactly and to its end."
src/CLI/Sync.jl:212-217 (plan()) — the same template body is rendered for every entry of vcat(INSTRUMENTS, ["gbg-doctor"])
src/CLI/Doctor.jl:772-784 (cmd_doctor) — gbg doctor only runs checks and prints pass/fail lines; never opens a round or prints a protocol/Workflow call
findings.description: Sync.plan renders the ONE SKILL.md.tmpl body for all five skills alike, varying only frontmatter and {{skill.command}}. The opening sentence matches Preflight.preflight's real behaviour for the four instrument skills, but is false for gbg-doctor, whose command is plain `gbg doctor`: cmd_doctor only runs the check suite and prints pass/warn/fail lines — it never opens a round, prints 'this instrument's protocol', or prints a Workflow call/next step. The template's own parenthetical concedes the round-opening claim is false for gbg-doctor but leaves the 'prints this instrument's protocol, the exact Workflow call and the next step' claim and the closing 'Follow the protocol printed above' line uncorrected, both still false in the rendered .claude/skills/gbg-doctor/SKILL.md shipped to every consumer. Failure scenario: a consumer running /gbg-doctor is told by the skill's own prose to follow a 'protocol' and 'Workflow call' that gbg doctor never prints — its real output is only a PASS/WARN/FAIL checklist.
findings.resolution_hint: Give SKILL.md.tmpl a doctor-specific branch or separate template describing gbg doctor's actual read-only check-and-report behaviour instead of reusing the preflight-instrument paragraph with a single parenthetical patch.

findings.title: test-Project.toml.seed always writes a git rev source, breaking a dev-pinned consumer's first Pkg.instantiate()
locations: src/CLI/Init.jl:293-294 — seeds test/Project.toml via Sync.render(Sync.template("test-Project.toml.seed"), s) whenever the consumer isn't the tool root itself
src/CLI/Sync.jl:305-314 (subenv_entries) — branches to a path source when pin(cfg) == "dev", a branch the seed path never takes
src/CLI/Init.jl:317 — "Next: `julia --project=docs -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.instantiate()'` (and test/), then `gbg sync`."
findings.description: subenv_entries, the function gbg sync uses to (re)write every sub-environment's tool entry, correctly switches to a local path source when the config's pin is the literal "dev" (schema/config.schema.json admits "dev" only for "tool root and fixture only"). But the one-time seed at gbg init writes test/Project.toml directly from test-Project.toml.seed via plain Sync.render, which always substitutes {{tool.url}}/v{{tool.version}}, so it always emits a git-rev [sources] entry even for the fixture, the one non-tool-root consumer that is dev-pinned. That yields rev = "vdev", not a resolvable git ref. init's own final message tells the operator to run Pkg.instantiate() for test/ BEFORE gbg sync (the step that would later fix the entry), so the very first instantiate a dev-pinned consumer is told to run fails to resolve GBGCodingTools. Failure scenario: gbg init --migrate seeds the fixture (pin = "dev"); its printed next step tells the operator to run Pkg.instantiate() for test/ before gbg sync; test/Project.toml's freshly seeded [sources] reads rev = "vdev", which Pkg cannot resolve, so Pkg.instantiate() errors before gbg sync ever corrects the entry.
findings.resolution_hint: Have Init.jl build test/Project.toml's tool entries via Sync.subenv_entries(cfg, "test") (as gbg sync does) instead of substituting them from the static test-Project.toml.seed slots, or reorder init's printed instructions so gbg sync runs before the test-environment Pkg.instantiate().

findings.title: make.jl.seed's deploydocs-guard comment describes a check that can never distinguish its two cases
locations: templates/make.jl.seed:4-5 — "It returns nothing when an open round of a docs instrument froze the build ...: that is exit 0, not a failure, so guard any deploydocs call on the value it returns."
ext/GBGCodingToolsDocumenterExt.jl (makedocs) — frozen path returns nothing; success path returns Documenter.makedocs(; kwargs...)'s own result
~/.julia/packages/Documenter/AXNMp/src/makedocs.jl:274,286 — function makedocs(; debug = false, ...); return debug ? document : nothing end
templates/make.jl.seed:9-17 — the seeded call passes no debug keyword
findings.description: The comment tells a consumer to guard any deploydocs(...) call on GBGCodingTools.makedocs's return value, on the premise a frozen (skipped) build is distinguishable from a real one by that value. But the success path returns whatever Documenter.makedocs(; kwargs...) returns, and Documenter.makedocs itself returns nothing unless debug = true is passed (confirmed in the installed Documenter source). The seed's own call passes no debug keyword, so under the exact template every consumer starts from, a normal successful build also returns nothing — identical to the frozen-skip path's explicit return nothing. A consumer who follows the comment literally would silently never deploy on any build, successful or frozen. Failure scenario: a consumer adds deploydocs(...) guarded as result === nothing || deploydocs(...); every ordinary successful docs build also returns nothing (Documenter's own default with no debug kwarg), so deploydocs never runs and the site never deploys, with no error anywhere.
findings.resolution_hint: Pass debug = true in the seed's call so a real build returns a non-nothing Document distinguishable from the frozen-skip nothing (and say so in the comment), or replace the return-value guard with an explicit signal such as checking GBGCodingTools.frozen_rounds(cfg, ...) directly in make.jl.seed before calling deploydocs.
